title: `cat <<END`<newline>`a`<newline>`EN`: completing on a heredoc terminator line puts the two shells on entirely different screens

observed.detail: diverges at step #1 ('tab'); first diff row 0 col 0; 24 row(s) differ
observed.notes: Both shells answer the Enter with PS2 — the buffer is deliberately incomplete at the newline, so nothing executes and the completion fires inside the continuation. The single-line control below completes the same word with the newline removed and PASSES, which is what makes the CONTINUATION the variable rather than the word. Every one of the 24 rows differs. zsh lists shell functions, a parameter block and a files block; zshrs still shows the three typed lines and four `_describe:compdescribe` rows and no listing. The round-3 note described this cell as `ZSH_EVAL_CONTEXT differing by a loadautofunc frame`; that specific comparison did NOT survive contact here — zsh's parameter listing does show `ZSH_EVAL_CONTEXT ///////// shfunc:loadautofunc:shfunc:shfunc:` (row 20), but zshrs produced no parameter listing at all, so there was no zshrs value to compare it against. What is pinned is the screen divergence that was observed.

controls.note: `cat EN` on one line — the same word completed outside a heredoc: PASSES.
